text: David Lewis's modal realism (On the Plurality of Worlds, 1986) holds that possible worlds are:
choices: maximal consistent sets of propositions — abstract objects
useful fictions with no ontological status
concrete, spatiotemporally isolated universes, as real as the actual world
mental constructions in the mind of God
explanation: Lewis's modal realism takes possible worlds to be concrete, spatiotemporally isolated universes exactly as real as ours — the actual world being merely the one we inhabit — which provokes the 'incredulous stare.' Option A is ersatzism (Plantinga, Adams, Stalnaker); the fictionalist and theistic readings (B, D) are not Lewis's view.
